The essential control is heterogeneous retention coefficients r_i versus a uniform coefficient r̄ = mean(r_i), with identical non-gate weights, architecture, data order, optimizer and training budget. Match retention probabilities, not average biases or timescales: these are nonlinear transformations. For fixed gates and the direct memory path, heterogeneous retention after k steps is mean(r_i^k); uniform retention is mean(r_i)^k. For r_i ∈ [0,1] and integer k > 1, Jensen’s inequality makes the former larger, strictly so with nonzero variance. Thus equal one-step mean retention still permits a longer memory tail. This mathematical implication does not establish useful learned memory; input-dependent gates, recurrent coupling and readout weights complicate actual dynamics. [Chrono initialization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11188) motivates distributing initial memory timescales.

Retention near one also saturates sigmoid gates: derivative r(1−r) becomes small, potentially preserving gradients along the state path while slowing gate adaptation. Heterogeneity therefore changes optimization as well as memory. Recommended controls include several uniform-retention settings, frozen versus trainable gates, and measurements of realized gate distributions, saturation, lag sensitivity and learning curves. [Gu et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/gu20a.html) explicitly address this saturation–learnability tradeoff. An initialization-only intervention can demonstrate a lasting training benefit, but cannot alone establish an advantage of maintained heterogeneity.

The located literature does not establish heterogeneous-versus-mean-matched uniform retention benefits in controlled GRU sequential recommendation. Chrono results on general sequence tasks do not supply that evidence. [GRU4Rec’s top-k study](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03847) demonstrates recommendation improvements from losses and sampling, not retention heterogeneity. A claim beyond a mean-retention shift therefore requires the matched recommendation ablation itself.
